cards.text: Paul is writing a letter to the believers in Galatia, and friend, this part gets PERSONAL. He starts by taking them back to the days before they knew God.

cards.question: Before they knew God, the Galatians were ___ to things that by nature are not gods.

cards.text: But now they know God. Then Paul fixes it: or rather, they are known by God. Knowing about somebody is nice, but being KNOWN by Him? That's a whole different batch.

cards.question: Now that the Galatians know God, what does Paul say they're doing?

answers.text: Turning back to weak and worthless principles
Running ahead without their church leaders
Holding back from helping the poor around them

cards.question: Paul asks the Galatians if they want to be enslaved by those weak and worthless principles all over again.

cards.text: Then Paul stops talking in general and names something the Galatians are actually doing. He's not guessing, friend. He's got receipts.

cards.question: What does Paul say the Galatians are observing?

answers.text: Special days and months and seasons and years
Strict rules about what to eat and drink
Washing their hands before every single meal

cards.question: Paul tells the Galatians he fears for them. What is he afraid of?

answers.text: That his efforts for them were in vain
That they will never write back to him
That they will run him out of town

cards.text: Then Paul pleads with them: "I beg you, brothers, become like me, for I became like you."

cards.question: Paul tells the Galatians they have done him wrong.

cards.text: Then Paul takes them back to the first time he preached the gospel to them. Spoiler, friend: it was NOT his best day.

cards.question: Paul reminds the Galatians why he first preached the gospel to them. What was the reason?

cards.text: Paul's illness was a trial to them. Most folks see a sick guest coming up the walk and suddenly remember they left the oven on, but the Galatians didn't despise him or reject him.

cards.question: Paul was sick when he came, but the Galatians didn't reject him. How did they welcome him?

answers.text: As if he were an angel of God
As if he were a king of Israel
As if he were a long lost brother

cards.question: Paul says the Galatians welcomed him as if he were Christ Jesus Himself.

cards.text: Paul is still thinking about how the Galatians first welcomed him. Now he asks them, "What then has become of your blessing?" Back then, he says, they would have given him something nobody can give, if it were possible.

cards.question: If it were possible, what does Paul say the Galatians would have given him back then?

cards.text: Their own EYES, friend. The best offer I ever got back in the junk drawer was a dead battery swearing it still had a little charge, and now Paul asks the Galatians a hard question.

cards.question: Paul asks if he has now become the Galatians' ___ by telling them the truth.

cards.text: Then Paul talks about some other people. He says those people are zealous for the Galatians, but not in a good way.

cards.question: Paul says those people aren't zealous for the Galatians in a good way. What do they want to do?

answers.text: Cut the Galatians off from Paul
Send the Galatians to help Paul
Bring the Galatians back to Paul

cards.question: Paul says those people want the Galatians to be zealous for them.

cards.text: You know the type: the coworker who's suddenly your BEST friend, but only if you leave your old group chat and join theirs. Then Paul has something to say about being zealous itself.

cards.question: Paul tells the Galatians that being zealous is never a good thing.

cards.text: Then Paul calls the Galatians his children. And he says he's going through something for them all over again.

cards.question: Paul calls the Galatians his children. What pains does he say he's in for them again?

answers.text: The pains of a long fast

cards.question: How long does Paul say he'll be in those pains for the Galatians?

answers.text: Until Christ is formed in them
Until he sees them face to face
Until they send word back to him

cards.text: AGAIN, friend! I get grumpy when my oven timer goes off twice, and Paul is signing up for round two of THIS.

cards.question: Paul says he wishes he could be with the Galatians right now. What would he change?

cards.text: Why? Because, he says, he's perplexed about them. But he still calls them his children, and I bet he hasn't stopped hoping.
